thread.title: The Long Night Of Value Investors

author: Compounding Cash
title: The Long Night Of Value Investors
text:
Last year I started to research and buy stocks after 10 years of pure index fund investing.
In my first overview in January I shared how my portfolio had beaten the index funds by 11% over 6 months, but I know how easy it is to get lucky in the short term. That doesn't mean long-term results will be just as good.
In the 3 months since then, my stocks have outperformed the index funds by another 4%. Most of that gain came in the last week of April.
This shows how easy it is to miss big returns! Up until that week, the total return was as much as 10% lower.
Through most of the quarter, Home Capital ( OTCPK:HMCBF ) and Aimia ( OTCPK:GAPFF ) were dragging down results while stocks like Netflix ( NFLX ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Shopify ( SHOP ), and Twilio ( TWLO ) were powering the returns. A quick rise in Aimia right at the end of the month allowed me to post good results.
My biggest holdings are value-oriented and we have seen lots of commentary about how badly value stocks have done this decade . The lag in my portfolio for most of the quarter reinforced this.
Nonetheless the opportunities are compelling enough that I will wait for them to produce results. If their stock prices don't rise, they could have large dividend payouts or very favourable share buybacks. Some could even deliver a profit by selling the whole business, but I believe they are worth more to me if they don't.
I'm not counting on a stock price recovery. All of my biggest holdings are actively looking at (or already doing) other ways to reward shareholders.
I'll need a few more years to tell if these good results are luck or skill. But I am getting more confident in some of my new stocks.
Keeping Up The Growth As always, my goal for these stocks is to average returns of 15% per year. I keep most of them in a TFSA account (like a Roth IRA) to avoid most taxes.
In the last 3 months, I've nearly doubled the amount invested in individual stocks. Doing more research increased my confidence. Now I'm trying to keep the portfolio more steady. I would like to invest more in some of these great opportunities, but I want to give it more time to prove itself.
That may be hard to do since my top picks just seem to keep getting more attractive.
I'm still trying to figure out a strategy for adding to positions. If a stock is good and the price drops, it makes sense to buy more. It's all but impossible to call the bottom so this could be the next best thing.
On the other hand, if it really is on the way down, that's just making it worse. And I certainly don't want to miss out on buying a good stock just because the price is 10% too high, then watch it go on to a 300% return.
Right now my plan is no plan. I'll watch what happens, do what seems right, and try to work out a good strategy.
Top Holdings Aimia: +15.9% total return
I've owned these shares less than 3 months and they have had many ups and downs. The volatility is almost on the level of Bitcoin ( OTCQX:GBTC ). I interrupted my initial research for a last-minute snowboarding trip and came back to find the price down by 50%. That's when I first bought shares. Since then I have picked up a lot more at significantly lower prices. The business is starting to show signs of the transition that will allow it to survive, but it may need a year or two to really show more value. The potential could be anywhere from a 2x to 10x return so this is my biggest position.
Home Capital: +3.9%
This has fallen quite a bit in the last 3 months despite an earnings report confirming the recovery of the business. I managed to buy a few shares below my earlier price. I also set some orders at even lower prices but didn't hit those. There may be a dividend or share buyback announcement later this year so more low prices would be appreciated! I think these shares could possibly double from current levels.
CBL ( CBL ): -1.8%
This position also grew a lot during the quarter - from my purchases, not the market performance. It's my third-largest position and I may add more. CBL has faced a lot of bad news, but after digging in, I saw a lot of signs that problems may be confined to a relatively short time and the business has options to move forward. CBL shares could gain 3 - 5x from their price today. And if they maintain their 20% dividend, that will help too. I expect the first signs of a turnaround in the next 12 months.
Washington Prime Group ( WPG ): -0.1%
WPG has many things in common with CBL. Its multiple is a little higher and its debt challenges are a little smaller. I don't know which one has better potential as a stock. WPG might be able to accelerate the internal results a little faster but it's already priced for better results. In the end I'm putting more on CBL because it's so cheap.
Amazon: +58.6%
I've never written a number that big for anything I've owned less than a year! But if Amazon is destroying malls, then surely it can diversify my investments. All of my biggest positions are stock with low multiples that I will happily sell at higher prices. I plan to keep Amazon for much longer. I expect them to do far more than I expect.
Shopify: +51.84%
This is another long-term holding. The market position is strong, the metrics are good, and the business model works well. I could have made a little profit trading around the recent 25% drop but I would hate to miss out on a 200% gain trying to do that!
Priceline (NASDAQ: BKNG ): +22.8%
The stock is now called Booking, but it has the same profitable business model. As a well-run company that's shown a lot of growth in EPS, this could be a good long-term holding. I haven't had a chance to do a lot of research so I would consider selling this if I see good returns and a better opportunity. Despite the fact that I own only one share, it's still among my top 7 positions!
Google ( GOOGL ): -5.6%
Google's stock is no secret and I'm not one of the early investors. But with a dominant market position it will be hard for anyone to challenge their profits for a long time. Even as Apple becomes more relevant in mobile and Facebook becomes more relevant in relationships, Google keeps control of one of the main places people go to find out where they can spend their money. My biggest fear is that the price won't get any cheaper.
Netflix: +71.4%
It's hard to believe I've held this for less than 12 months but Netflix has done well. It's still a very small position for me. After more consideration I would be open to adding to that position even at these prices. I think it could still double or more from here.
Other Holdings The new additions have outweighed some of my other important holdings. I'm hoping to see some drops in the prices to help me buy more. Instead most of them have moved up.
Cenovus ( CVE ) Athabasca ( OTCPK:ATHOF ) -- bought and then closed for a quick 30% profit (with another 25% price gain after I sold it) Constellation Software ( OTCPK:CNSWF ) Fairfax ( OTCPK:FRFHF ) Fairfax India ( OTCPK:FFXDF ) Berkshire ( BRK.A )( BRK.B ) Fiat Chrysler ( FCAU ) GM ( GM ) Southwest ( LUV ) Delta ( DAL ) Air Canada ( OTCQX:ACDVF ) Seritage ( SRG ) Apple ( AAPL ) Facebook ( FB ) I have a few smaller positions that are just experiments. Some of them are posting good returns but I can't claim that I knew much about that!
Major Changes I added Aimia after reading a comment from a reader on my last portfolio update. With some research I saw a lot of potential to get bigger returns than Home Capital (my previous largest position). I've kept adding more until it became my largest position. If the prices go even lower I'll make it even larger.
I also started increasing CBL and WPG. I previously had very small positions but as I learned more and their stock prices fell, I bought into the value of their cashflow. They have complex financial structures and I'll need to learn more about them. If I knew enough to fully confirm what I've seen, I could put one or both of them among my largest positions.
I sold my position in Twilio ( TWLO ). I originally bought it because the stock had fallen pretty far last year. It recently gained 50% on my purchase price. At those levels I don't have an extremely high confidence in its future growth. It's a good business but I can't justify it as well as my other holdings. After selling it the price rose nearly 30% -- by now it would have been my largest percentage gain and close to doubling my purchase price.
This extra gain wasn't unexpected but I didn't have enough confidence in the business to bet on its long-term growth. Great investors such as Mohnish Pabrai will tell you about the many stocks that have done well after they sold them.
It's just part of the market - the cheaper stocks have a lower level of risk so I have to re-allocate my capital and forgo some of those gains. The momentum of a recovering stock can carry it higher but when I can't tell whether a stock will gain 10% or 10x it's not worth the risk of having the price fall back.
Up Next: Do Nothing? I'm trying not to add more stocks or increase my positions now. Instead I'll buy more of the index funds to keep a balanced portfolio and not bet too much of my net worth on this. But if prices fall a lot, I may not be able to resist!
On the other hand, if some of the smaller positions gain enough, I may sell out of them and hold the cash for the next buying opportunity.
I'm focusing most of my research on the quarterly updates and other news from the top 3 positions. Other than that, I'm happy to apply my indexing strategy here - walk away and do nothing.
Disclosure: I am/we are long ALL OF THE ABOVE.
